title: Fruit and Vegetables Part - 1 Mock Test

questions.question: Which of the following is a common physiological disorder in mango?
questions.explanation: Black tip and malformation are major physiological disorders in mango. Black tip is caused by air pollution, particularly fluoride, while malformation results from hormonal imbalance or pathogen attack.[cite: 21]

questions.question: Which mango variety is known for its distinct aroma and sweetness?
questions.explanation: Alphonso is one of the most famous mango varieties, known for its rich aroma, smooth texture, and sweet taste. It is widely grown in Maharashtra, India.[cite: 21]

questions.question: Which state in India is the largest producer of mangoes?
questions.explanation: Uttar Pradesh is the largest producer of mangoes in India, contributing significantly to the country's mango production.[cite: 21]

questions.question: The physiological disorder 'Spongy Tissue' is commonly found in which mango variety?
questions.explanation: Spongy tissue is a post-harvest disorder in Alphonso mangoes caused by improper ripening and temperature variations during storage.[cite: 21]

questions.question: Which of the following mango varieties is fiberless and suitable for making pulp and juice?
questions.explanation: Totapuri mango is fiberless, making it ideal for processing into pulp, juice, and mango-based products.[cite: 21]

questions.question: Which of the following is a dwarf hybrid mango variety?
questions.explanation: Amrapali is a dwarf hybrid mango variety developed by crossing Dashehari and Neelum. It is known for its high yield and deep orange pulp.[cite: 21]

questions.question: 'Jhumka' is a physiological disorder in mango caused by
questions.explanation: Jhumka is a mango disorder where the fruitlets remain small and fail to develop properly, often caused by hormonal imbalances or environmental factors.[cite: 21]

questions.question: Which mango variety is most commonly exported from India?
questions.explanation: Alphonso mango, grown mainly in Maharashtra, is the most exported Indian mango due to its superior taste, aroma, and texture.[cite: 21]

questions.question: Which of the following physiological disorders in mango is associated with poor calcium translocation?
questions.explanation: Spongy tissue in mango is a physiological disorder caused by poor calcium translocation, leading to internal tissue breakdown in ripe fruits.[cite: 21]

questions.question: Which hybrid mango variety was developed by crossing Rumani and Neelum?
questions.explanation: Arka Puneet is a hybrid mango variety developed by crossing Rumani and Neelum. It is known for its attractive color and excellent taste.[cite: 21]

questions.question: Which of the following mango varieties is known for its naturally long shelf life?
questions.explanation: Neelum mango is known for its long shelf life, making it suitable for storage and transport over long distances.[cite: 21]

questions.question: Which hybrid mango variety was developed by crossing Dashehari and Neelum?
questions.explanation: Amrapali is a dwarf hybrid variety developed by crossing Dashehari and Neelum. It is known for its high yield and deep orange pulp.[cite: 21]

questions.question: The hybrid mango variety 'Arka Puneet' is a cross of which two parent varieties?
questions.explanation: Arka Puneet is a hybrid developed from Rumani and Neelum, known for its attractive color and disease resistance.[cite: 21]

questions.question: Which hybrid mango variety is known for being semi-dwarf and has a seedless tendency?
questions.explanation: Sindhu is a hybrid mango variety derived from Ratna (Neelum x Alphonso) x Alphonso and is known for its seedless tendency.[cite: 21]

questions.question: The hybrid variety 'PKM-1' is a cross of which mango varieties?
questions.explanation: PKM-1 is a hybrid variety developed by crossing Chinnasuvarnarekha x Neelum, known for its good yield and medium-sized fruits.[cite: 21]

questions.question: Which of the following banana varieties is best suited for processing into banana powder and baby food?
questions.explanation: Rasthali is a highly preferred variety for making banana powder and baby food due to its sweet taste, fine texture, and high nutrient content.[cite: 21]

questions.question: What is the scientific reason why the "Grand Nain" variety is preferred for commercial cultivation worldwide?

options.a: It has a long shelf life and high productivity
options.b: It is the sweetest banana variety
options.c: It requires less water for growth
options.d: It has a unique red color
options.e: It is a wild banana variety

questions.explanation: The Grand Nain variety is widely cultivated because of its high yield, disease resistance, uniform fruit size, and longer shelf life, making it ideal for export.[cite: 21]

questions.question: In which banana variety is "Natural Parthenocarpy" (fruit development without fertilization) commonly observed?
questions.explanation: Banana plants exhibit natural parthenocarpy, meaning their fruits develop without fertilization. This characteristic is found in various commercial varieties like Robusta, Poovan, Grand Nain, and Dwarf Cavendish.[cite: 21]

questions.question: During which months is banana planting generally done in hilly areas?
questions.explanation: In hilly regions, banana planting is best suited during August - September, as the moderate climate and adequate moisture help in better establishment and growth.[cite: 21]

questions.question: In which of the following months is banana commonly planted in plains?
questions.explanation: In plain areas, banana planting is usually done in January - February and November - December to take advantage of optimal soil moisture and temperature conditions for proper root establishment.[cite: 21]

questions.question: Which of the following pests affects the banana plant by damaging the banana plant's corm?
questions.explanation: The rhizome corm weevil, also known as the banana corm weevil, is a major pest of bananas. The adult female weevil lays eggs on the banana plant corm or pseudostem. These eggs hatch into grubs, which bore into the plant and feed on the internal tissues, causing significant damage.[cite: 21]

questions.question: Which of the following diseases in bananas is caused by a fungus and leads to yellowing and wilting of leaves?
questions.explanation: Panama Disease, caused by Fusarium oxysporum, is a soil-borne fungal disease that causes yellowing, wilting, and eventual death of banana plants.[cite: 21]

questions.question: The banana aphid is a vector for which serious viral disease in banana plants?
questions.explanation: Banana aphids (Pentalonia nigronervos) transmit Banana Bunchy Top Virus (BBTV), which causes stunted growth, bunched leaves, and severe yield loss.[cite: 21]

questions.question: Sigatoka leaf spot in banana plants is caused by which pathogen?
questions.explanation: Sigatoka leaf spot is a fungal disease caused by Mycosphaerella musicola (Yellow Sigatoka) and Mycosphaerella fijiensis (Black Sigatoka), leading to leaf necrosis and reduced photosynthesis.[cite: 21]

questions.question: What is the major symptom of Cigar End Rot disease in bananas?

options.c: Dark brown to black lesions on fruit tips

questions.explanation: Cigar End Rot is caused by Verticillium theobromae and Trachysphaera fructigena, leading to blackening and shriveling of the banana fruit tip, resembling a burned cigar.[cite: 21]

questions.question: What is the scientific name of Acid Lime?
questions.explanation: The scientific name of Acid Lime is Citrus aurantifolia, whereas Citrus sinensis is for sweet orange, Citrus limon for lemon, and Citrus reticulata for mandarins.[cite: 21]

questions.question: Which of the following is a recommended variety of Acid Lime?
questions.explanation: Kagzi Lime is one of the most widely grown varieties of Acid Lime in India, known for its thin skin and juicy pulp. The other options refer to different citrus fruits or mango varieties.[cite: 21]

questions.question: The variety "Phule Sharbati" is associated with which fruit?
questions.explanation: Phule Sharbati is a variety of Acid Lime developed for its superior juice content and adaptability to Indian climatic conditions.[cite: 21]

questions.question: Which of the following varieties of Acid Lime is developed by Tamil Nadu Agricultural University (TNAU)?
questions.explanation: PKM 1 (Periyakulam 1) is an improved variety of Acid Lime developed by TNAU, known for its high yield and disease resistance.[cite: 21]

questions.question: The variety "Phule Sharbati" was developed in which Indian state?
questions.explanation: Phule Sharbati is an Acid Lime variety developed by Mahatma Phule Krishi Vidyapeeth (MPKV), Maharashtra, known for its improved yield and better fruit quality.[cite: 21]

questions.question: The Acid Lime variety "Vikram" is mainly grown in which Indian region?
questions.explanation: Vikram is a variety of Acid Lime popular in Gujarat, known for its resistance to pests and diseases, along with high productivity.[cite: 21]

questions.question: What is the optimum soil pH range for growing Acid Lime?
questions.explanation: Acid Lime grows best in a neutral to slightly acidic soil with a pH range of 6.5-7.0. Highly alkaline or saline soils can negatively affect plant growth and fruit quality.[cite: 21]

questions.question: Which type of soil is best suited for Acid Lime cultivation?

options.b: Deep, well-drained medium black or loamy soil
options.d: Saline-alkaline soil with high calcium carbonate
options.e: Peaty soil with high organic matter

questions.explanation: Acid Lime grows well in deep, well-drained medium black, loamy, or alluvial soils rich in organic matter. Soils with high calcium carbonate content should be avoided.[cite: 21]

questions.question: During which months is Acid Lime typically planted?
questions.explanation: December - February & June - September are the recommended planting seasons for Acid Lime to ensure optimal root establishment and fruit development.[cite: 21]

questions.question: What is the approximate yield of Acid Lime per hectare per year?
questions.explanation: With good management practices, Acid Lime yields approximately 25 tonnes per hectare per year under optimal growing conditions.[cite: 21]

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a major pest of Acid Lime?
questions.explanation: Powdery Mildew is a fungal disease, not a pest. The main pests of Acid Lime include Fruit Sucking Moth, Shoot Borer, Fruit Fly, and Citrus Root Nematode.[cite: 21]

questions.question: Which disease causes small cankers (corky lesions) on the leaves, twigs, and fruits of Acid Lime?
questions.explanation: Citrus Canker, caused by Xanthomonas axonopodis, leads to corky, raised lesions on leaves, twigs, and fruits, reducing market quality.[cite: 21]

questions.question: What is the scientific name of Sweet Orange?
questions.explanation: The scientific name of Sweet Orange is Citrus sinensis, while Citrus aurantifolia refers to Acid Lime, Citrus aurantium to Bitter Orange, Citrus reticulata to Mandarin, and Citrus limon to Lemon.[cite: 21]

questions.question: "Sathgudi" is a famous variety of Sweet Orange grown in which Indian state?
questions.explanation: Sathgudi is a popular variety of Sweet Orange grown mainly in Andhra Pradesh, known for its excellent juice quality and sweetness.[cite: 21]

questions.question: Which variety of Sweet Orange is commonly known as "Mosambi" in India?
questions.explanation: Batavian Sweet Orange is commonly referred to as Mosambi in India, known for its low acid content and mild sweetness.[cite: 21]

questions.question: The "Malta Blood Red" variety of Sweet Orange is popular for which unique characteristic?
questions.explanation: Malta Blood Red is known for its red-colored pulp, caused by the presence of anthocyanins, which gives the fruit a distinct appearance and higher antioxidant content.[cite: 21]

questions.question: What is the ideal soil pH range for Sweet Orange cultivation?
questions.explanation: Sweet Orange grows best in slightly acidic to neutral soils, with an optimal pH range of 6.5-7.5. Alkaline or highly acidic soils can affect nutrient availability and tree health.[cite: 21]

questions.question: What is the ideal climatic condition for growing Sweet Orange?

options.b: Dry climate with moderate rainfall (50-75 cm) and well-defined summer & winter
options.c: Cold and frosty climate with low temperatures

questions.explanation: Sweet Orange requires a dry climate with moderate rainfall (50-75 cm) from June to September, along with well-defined summer and winter seasons for proper fruit development.[cite: 21]

questions.question: Which of the following is a major pest of Sweet Orange that causes serpentine tunnels on young leaves?
questions.explanation: Leaf Miner (Phyllocnistis citrella) is a major pest that creates serpentine tunnels on young leaves, leading to reduced photosynthesis and weak plant growth.[cite: 21]

questions.question: What is the scientific name of Grapes?
questions.explanation: Vitis vinifera is the scientific name of Grapes, whereas Citrus sinensis is for Sweet Orange, Musa paradisiaca for Banana, Mangifera indica for Mango, and Psidium guajava for Guava.[cite: 21]

questions.question: "Tas-A-Ganesh" is an improved variety developed from which grape cultivar?
questions.explanation: Tas-A-Ganesh is an improved variety of Thompson Seedless with larger berry size and better sweetness.[cite: 21]

questions.question: Which grape variety is known for its deep red color and large berry size?
questions.explanation: Red Globe is a famous table grape variety known for its large, deep red berries and sweet taste.[cite: 21]

questions.question: Which of the following is a seedless variety of Grapes?
questions.explanation: Thompson Seedless is one of the most popular seedless grape varieties used for fresh consumption and raisin production.[cite: 21]

questions.question: What type of climate is most suitable for grape cultivation?

options.b: Humid tropical climate with high rainfall
options.c: Dry and humid climate with moderate rainfall

questions.explanation: Grapes thrive best in a dry and humid climate with moderate rainfall (500-900 mm), as excessive moisture can lead to fungal diseases.[cite: 21]

questions.question: What is the ideal temperature range for grape cultivation?
questions.explanation: The ideal temperature range for grape cultivation is 15°C to 40°C, as extreme cold or heat can negatively impact growth, flowering, and fruit development.[cite: 21]

questions.question: Which type of soil is best suited for grape cultivation?

options.a: Heavy clay soil with poor drainage
options.d: Waterlogged soil with high organic matter
options.e: Peaty soil with high moisture retention

questions.explanation: Grapes grow best in deep, well-drained sandy loam soils, which provide good aeration and prevent root diseases caused by waterlogging.[cite: 21]

questions.question: Excessive rainfall (>900 mm) in grape cultivation can lead to which major problem?

options.c: Fungal diseases like powdery mildew and anthracnose

questions.explanation: Excessive rainfall (>900 mm) increases humidity, which promotes fungal diseases like powdery mildew, anthracnose, and downy mildew in grapevines.[cite: 21]

questions.question: What is the best-suited pH range for grape cultivation?
questions.explanation: Grapes prefer a soil pH of 6.5-7.5, which ensures optimal nutrient availability and healthy root development.[cite: 21]

questions.question: What is the best time for planting grape rootstocks?
questions.explanation: The best time for planting grape rootstocks is January - February, as the favorable climate conditions support early root establishment and healthy vine growth.[cite: 21]

questions.question: Which of the following is commonly used as a planting material in grape cultivation?
questions.explanation: Grapes are propagated using rootstocks, which provide disease resistance, better growth, and higher productivity compared to direct seed planting.[cite: 21]

questions.question: Which training system is commonly used in grapevine cultivation?
questions.explanation: The Pandal system (overhead trellis) is a traditional training system used in grape cultivation to support vine growth and improve sunlight exposure.[cite: 21]

questions.question: Which modern grapevine training system improves yield and quality?
questions.explanation: The Y-trellis system is an improved training method that provides better sunlight penetration, air circulation, and higher yield potential in grape cultivation.[cite: 21]

questions.question: Which of the following system is used to train the grape vine in grape cultivation?
questions.explanation: The Y-trellis system is an improved training method that provides better sunlight penetration, air circulation, and higher yield potential in grape cultivation.[cite: 21]

questions.question: What is the primary advantage of using rootstocks in grapevine cultivation?

options.b: Enhances disease resistance and soil adaptability

questions.explanation: Rootstocks are selected for their resistance to soil-borne diseases (like nematodes and root rot) and their ability to adapt to different soil types, leading to better vine health and yield.[cite: 21]

questions.question: When is pruning done for the summer crop of grapes?
questions.explanation: In grape cultivation, pruning for the summer crop is done in December - January to ensure better vegetative growth and fruit development for harvesting in April - May.[cite: 21]
